reason: Reproduced on transactions.group-menu: opening Group puts focus on the menu container, not a first item, but focus is inside the new layer, the menu sits right after its trigger in tab order, and one Tab reaches the only control, the Group by combobox, where ArrowDown moves the active option from To/From to Account. Focus order preserves meaning and operability, so 2.4.3 does not fail; first-item focus is an APG practice, not an A or AA requirement.
criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 Focus Order: focus moves into the opened menu (not left on the page), the menu follows the Group button in the tab order, and Tab then reaches the single control and exits to Sort, so the sequence preserves meaning and operability. 2.1.1 Keyboard: the Group by combobox is reachable with Tab and operable with ArrowDown. 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: the menu exposes role menu with name Group and the combobox exposes its name and expanded state; whether a menu role fits a panel with no menu items is a separate role-state question, not this focus-placement claim.

reason: Reproduced: the Group by input carries autocomplete="garbage", a deliberate autofill-suppression value. The field picks how the table is grouped (To/From, Account, Card, Category) and collects nothing about the user, so 1.3.5 does not apply and no A or AA criterion fails.
criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and serve a purpose in the Input Purposes list; Group by is a view control with options To/From, Account, Card, Category, GL Code, so the criterion does not apply. 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: the ax probe shows role combobox, name Group by, expanded=true, haspopup=listbox; the invalid token changes none of them. 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions: a visible Group by label is attached to the input. HTML validity is not an AA criterion since 4.1.1 was removed in WCAG 2.2.
